03 · Color roles

Not grouped as primary, secondary, accent: these colors carry meaning, not hierarchy. Hex and the custom property name are read back from each swatch's own computed style, not typed in twice.

Page

#fbfbfc · --color-page

The reading surface. White, never warm.

Panel

#efeff1 · --color-panel

Raised blocks sitting on the page. Always bordered: the tint alone is 1.11 contrast against the page and will not define an edge on its own.

Rule

#d8d8dc · --color-rule

Hairlines. Never text.

Muted

#67676e · --color-muted

Metadata.

Body

#35353b · --color-body

Running copy.

Jet

#08080a · --color-jet

Headlines and default prose ink, and Robotics. Also the confidence rule, in all three line styles, regardless of what color the numeral above it is set in.

Blue deep

#101f52 · --color-blue-deep

Structure and chart outlines, and Space.

Blue bright

#1f5fe0 · --color-blue-bright

Links, and AI. The tightest value in the system at 4.85 on panel: never long copy, never below 12px.

Crimson

#b3122b · --color-crimson

Emphasis and kickers, and Energy.

06 · The heading map

Demonstrated, not described: this is the section that would have caught the article title bug. Labels name what each element is set in rather than making an editorial claim, because voice is not delegable and this is a token demonstration, not a piece.

An article title, set in `title`, the same step as the Articles lead.

Body copy immediately under the title, set in `body`, running copy at seventeen pixels.

A section head, set in `head`, dividing the piece.

Body copy under a section head, still `body`.

A subhead, set in `subhead`, dividing the section.

Body copy under a subhead. Nothing in an article body goes below `subhead`; a piece that needs a fourth level is structured wrong.

The 64ch measure, filled with the real seed article's real body, rendered through the same MDX pipeline the article route uses, so the line breaks below are the ones a reader actually gets.

Placeholder body. It exists to show how a marked figure sits inside a sentence and to give the numeral lint something real to run against. It is not an argument and nobody should read it as one.

The pitch is free cooling and uninterrupted sun. The bill is launch mass. Announced capacity across the credible proposals sits at 0.0GW, against contracted capacity of 0GW. Announced, contracted, and energized are three different numbers wearing one word, and saying which one you mean is most of the work.

An inset panel. Assumptions, denominators, and anything a reader can skip without losing the argument.

The implied cost per delivered watt works out to $00.00/W on the most generous assumptions available, and the assumptions are doing most of the work. That figure is dotted because Burn Rate did the arithmetic, which is the only reason anything is ever dotted.

Every figure above is a placeholder rather than a record, which is why each one is visibly fake. When the fact store has real entries these become record ids and the marks stop being decoration.

Until someone publishes delivered watts per kilogram on orbit, every projection in this category is an argument about physics dressed as a financial model.
